lastQuery: <task> Perform a READ-ONLY code review of the magomap backend in /home/motoko/workspace/magomap. Do not edit files, do not commit, do not change the git index or HEAD. Running tests is allowed: pnpm -r test; Postgres tests need TEST_DATABASE_URL=postgres://magomap:magomap@localhost:5432/magomap_test (container is running). Scope: commits f25c52c..0b2f21f on main (plan 01: all 7 tasks plus a fix commit after a first review). Skip pnpm-lock.yaml and assets/. What it is: pnpm monorepo. - packages/domain: wire types, zod schemas, deterministic ids, a did this place move? rule. - packages/db: Kysely connector for Cloudflare D1, Postgres (via Hyperdrive) and better-sqlite3; migrations for both dialects; stores for users/sessions, offline sync push/pull, chunked Kakao import. - apps/api: Hono Cloudflare Worker with Kakao OAuth sign-in, sync, import and search routes. Review against: - Plan: docs/superpowers/plans/2026-11-19-01-magomap-backend.md (Global Constraints, Review Focus, each task) - Spec: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-19-magomap-design.md - Build process: docs/superpowers/build-process.md Most important guarantee: no diary entry (visit_notes) or link may ever be lost or silently overwritten. Consider sync, import, clock skew, two devices of one user pushing at once, and deleted places. Also check: - Cloudflare limits: max 100 bound parameters per statement, max 1 MB JSON parameter, about 50 statements per request, Free plan CPU budget. - Same behaviour on SQLite/D1 and Postgres. - Every query scoped by user. - Auth and session handling secure. A first review already found and fixed issues in 0b2f21f: import vs concurrent note edits, Postgres-unsafe text, tombstones for deletes before creates, place write races, clock clamping, superseded mutation status, incomplete imports, redirect handling, chunk size cap. Verify those fixes are correct and look for anything that review missed. </task> <grounding_rules> Every finding must be anchored in code you read; give file:line. Mark hypotheses as such. Prefer running a test or reproducing to confirm. </grounding_rules> <structured_output_contract> Report findings ranked Critical / Important / Minor. Each finding: file:line, what is wrong, a concrete failing scenario, and a fix. End with a verdict. </structured_output_contract> <dig_deeper_nudge> After the first pass, look for second-order issues: races between two devices, partial failure mid-batch, and dialect differences. </dig_deeper_nudge>
